Humans are also capable of inserting cis-double bonds either ﬁve or six carbons from the carboxyl carbon of a FA (D5 desaturase
and D6 desaturase activity, respectively). These activities, when combined with FA elongation pathways, form a powerful mecha-
nism for synthesis of highly polyunsaturated FAs such as 20:4u6 or 22:6u3 from dietary essential FAs. The conversion of 18:3u3 to
22:6u3 also theoretically requires a D4 desaturase to insert the 6th double bond (in 22:5u3); however, humans lack this enzyme. It
is now believed that 22:5u3 is elongated to 24:5u3, converted to 24:6u3 by D6 desaturase, and ﬁnally chain-shortened to 22:6u3 by
one cycle of peroxisomal b-oxidation.
Fatty acids as components of complex lipids
FAs are important building blocks for various cellular complex lipids (Fig. 7) (reviewed in Nguyen et al., 2008). For simplicity, the
pathways for incorporation of FAs into these lipids are outlined only brieﬂy. In most cases, fatty acyl-CoA and not free FA partic-
ipates in these biosynthetic reactions. Nearly all cells synthesize phospholipids, which are essential membrane constituents.
